questions.stem: In triangle OAB, OA = a and OB = b. M is the midpoint of AB. Express OM in terms of a and b.
questions.explanation: OM = OA + AM = a + 1/2 AB = a + 1/2(b − a) = a + 1/2 b − 1/2 a = 1/2 a + 1/2 b = 1/2(a + b). Option (a) gives AM, not OM.

questions.stem: OABC is a parallelogram with OA = a and OC = c. Point P lies on OB such that OP = 2/3 OB. Express OP in terms of a and c.
questions.explanation: In a parallelogram, OB = OA + AB = a + c. So OP = 2/3 OB = 2/3(a + c) = 2/3 a + 2/3 c.

questions.stem: OA = 2a and OB = 2b. Point X lies on AB such that AX:XB = 1:3. Express OX in terms of a and b.
In triangle OPQ, OP = p and OQ = q. R is the point on PQ such that PR:RQ = 2:1. Express OR in terms of p and q.
questions.explanation: OR = OP + PR = p + 2/3 PQ = p + 2/3(q − p) = p + 2/3 q − 2/3 p = 1/3 p + 2/3 q. Since R is 2/3 of the way along PQ, its position vector is weighted towards Q.

questions.stem: OA = a and OB = b. OC = 3a − 2b. Find AC in terms of a and b, and determine the relationship between AC and AB.

options.text: AC = 4a − 2b, not a multiple of AB

questions.explanation: AC = OC − OA = (3a − 2b) − a = 2a − 2b. AB = b − a. So AC = −2(b − a) = −2 AB. Since AC is a scalar multiple of AB, points A, B and C are collinear, with C on the opposite side of A from B.
